locked_prediction.decision_rule: a coordinate is declared load-bearing if its pooled Holm p < 0.05 AND its effect points the same direction in at least 4 of 7 items
locked_prediction.directional: NONE. The PD direction was derivable because every item presents a claim under a stated arrangement, mapping onto PD's process/outcome definition. No comparable mapping exists for these eight, so the test is two-sided and the rule requires only a difference.
locked_prediction.expected_outcome: Phase 5's post-hoc correlations found no coordinate besides PD surviving Holm in any designation, and no stable ordering across designations. A null across all eight is a plausible and informative result.
locked_prediction.failure_condition: If no coordinate survives, the finding is that PD is the only load-bearing coordinate of the ten under this method, on this item set and model. Reported as such, not reframed.
locked_prediction.items_not_trimmed: Three of the seven items showed small effects under the PD manipulation. They are RETAINED. Cutting them would save ~40% and would bias the sweep toward coordinates behaving like PD.
locked_prediction.primary: per coordinate, the paired C+ vs C- contrast on the share of decisions classifying `good`, Holm-corrected over all eight pooled contrasts as one family
locked_prediction.question: Which of the remaining eight coordinates move the deterministic good/bad headline when pinned to their endpoints?
locked_prediction.what_a_survivor_means: that pinning the coordinate on its own label moves the outcome. It does NOT yet show the LABEL carries it rather than the numeral; that needs the swap control label_semantics_r1 ran for PD, which is the correct follow-up for survivors.

analysis.primary_test: per coordinate, pooled Holm p < 0.05 over all eight contrasts as one family, AND the effect pointing the same direction in at least 4 of 7 items

payload.note: Deterministic choice counts under stipulated standards. No moral label is assigned and no moral quality is measured.

limits: All items share the same asymmetric payoff structure (1 vs −5 for the individual; −4 vs +2 for the group), which may reveal a within-design pattern to attentive participants.

The 'protect the individual right-holder' option is always named first and framed around possession/prior claim, while the 'override' option is always second; consistent ordering could introduce a primacy or status-quo bias.
Item 05 involves a mandatory rest slot, which carries implicit labour-law salience that the other items lack, potentially making it non-equivalent to the rest of the set.
